newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK interbank boosted on hopes of U.S. rate hike.
newsitem.headline: HK interbank boosted on hopes of U.S. rate hike.

text.p: Hong Kong's interbank market edged up on Friday on expectation of an interest rate hike in the United States next week, dealers said.
The overnight interbank market ended the morning session at 5-5/16 1/4 percent against 5-3/16 1/4 percent on Thursday while three months stood at 5-3/4 11/16 versus 5-5/8 9/16 percent.
"It's gone up because people are now more hopeful than ever of the FOMC raising interest rates," a dealer with a Japanese bank said.
The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC), the Federal Reserve's policy setting arm, meets on Tuesday next week.

The dealer said overnight U.S. data showing a fall in recent jobless claims and bullish housing figures aided hopes that interest rates would be raised. Another dealer noted demand was also typically boosted ahead of the weekend.
Expectations of higher rates caused demand for government bills and notes to ease and yields to rise, dealers said.

The one-week bill yielded 5.04 percent against 5.00 percent on Thursday while the seven-year Exchange Fund note yielded 7.68 percent against 7.60 percent, five-year 7.36 percent versus 7.30 percent and three-year 6.72 percent against 6.65 percent.
